ai.description: This toad reaches 6–8 cm. It is brown with darker mottling and a pale vertebral stripe. Key features include a small tympanum, warty skin, and prominent parotoid glands. Family: Bufonidae.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Southern Hill Toad is best distinguished by its lack of cranial crests and the presence of a distinct, enlarged, kidney-shaped parotoid gland behind each eye.
ai.habitat: The Southern Hill Toad inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations ranging from 600 to 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Southern Hill Toad is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates among leaf litter and rocky outcrops in its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Duttaphrynus microtympanum* is an oviparous breeder that lays long, gelatinous strings of eggs in water. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Southern Hill Toad is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily inhabiting high-elevation evergreen forests in Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
ai.callDescription: The Southern Hill Toad produces a low-pitched, rhythmic trill that sounds like a mechanical buzzing, typically heard near rocky streams or damp forest habitats.
